clauses.reason: Statutory pay systems: sets the rates of basic pay of the statutory pay systems on the attached schedules. Ends when EO 12826 (signed 1992-12-30; 57 FR 62909, Federal Register of December 31, 1992) in its Sec. 7: supersedes EO 12786: "Executive Order No. 12786 of December 26, 1991, is superseded." The sentence carries no delayed-effective-date wording of its own, so the end is the signing date, 1992-12-30. Alternative reading disclosed: the successor order's own schedules take effect on the first day of the first pay period on or after January 1, 1993, so the rates of this order may be read as governing pay until then; that moment is not a single stated date, and the express supersession sentence is the first held instrument ending the order.

Supersedes EO 12736 of December 12, 1990. A supersession of a whole earlier order is a one-time act; the order states no effective date for this sentence (Sec. 6 fixes dates only for the schedules), so it was performed on signing, 1991-12-26, and the command is exhausted on that date. A later supersession of EO 12786 does not change when this one-time command was performed.

research_rationale:
EO 12786 of December 26, 1991 (Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay and Allowances), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 67453, Federal Register of December 30, 1991; machine-extracted text layer; the schedule tables are OCR and partly garbled). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1991-12-26). The order sets pay-system schedules (Sec. 1 to 4 and Schedules 1 to 8), interim geographic adjustments (Sec. 5 and Schedule 9), effective dates (Sec. 6) and supersedes EO 12736 (Sec. 7). Inventory: the dossier's 28 clauses (Sec. 1 to 7 with their subsections, Schedules 1 to 9 and a second Schedule 8 segment) cover the operative text; the enacting formula is not a separate command. EO 12826 (signed 1992-12-30) supersedes it expressly in its Sec. 7. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 1. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number are its own text and EO 12826, which is the superseding order.
